thread:
maria: heads up — bringing up the new 13B-int6 candidate (build 2026-03-18). observed two things in the smoke tests: a 95th/99th tail latency spike on long-context prompts (~4k tokens) and a subtle quality dip on our summarization eval (ROUGE-L down ~0.9 pts). need quick cost-vs-quality guidance for product + GTN. any ideas?
ashok: can you paste the perf histogram and the eval sample that regressed?
maria: pasted below. perf snapshot (from local perf-run):
```
model: redwood-13b-int6-cand
p50: 58ms
p95: 420ms
p99: 980ms
mean: 120ms
context: 4k tokens, batch=1, kv-cache warmstart=false
cpu offload: disabled
```
and one failing summarization example (gold vs model):
```
input: long product doc (~3800 tokens)
expected: concise executive summary with 3 bullets
model output: repeats sections, loses global theme, shorter coverage
```
rebecca: that p99 is worrying for interactive flows. is int6 putting more pressure on memory movement or kernel fallback?
dan: likely quantization artifact + attention kernel pathing for long sequences. int6 dequant/quant steps can blow up CPU time if KV cache misses cause rematerialization. do we have profiling traces?
maria: ran a tracing build. snippet from runtime trace: 
```
[2026-03-18T15:12:03Z] attention_kernels: chosen_path=chunked_unfused_int6
[2026-03-18T15:12:03Z] kv_cache: miss_rate=0.28, fetch_latency_avg=12ms
[2026-03-18T15:12:03Z] fallback: quant_dequant_cpu_run started (130ms)
```
ashok: miss_rate 28% is high — explains dequant fallback runs hitting CPU. question: why KV cache warmstart false? product requests should be warmstarted in prod. if this repro uses cold startup, tails are expected but we need to quantify production impact.
samir: cost side: int6 reduces GPU memory and allows higher packing but if CPU fallbacks happen a lot the token cost increases. quick numbers: int8 baseline unit-cost = $0.0035 per 1k tokens, int6 steady-state might be $0.0021 per 1k tokens but with 25% fallback overhead cost becomes effectively $0.0029. so margin is small for long-tail workloads.
rebecca: quality: ROUGE-L -0.9 is small but directional. do we see specific failure modes? repetition and missing coverage suggests attention precision loss. could be fixed by small learning-time calibration (LLM quant aware fine-tune) or by switching to int8 for long contexts.
maria: product asks: can we have a simple rollout policy that prefers int6 by default but routes long-context or high-recall routes to int8/float? want recommendations we can give GTN.
ashok: propose hybrid routing rules:
- route if input_length > 2048 -> int8 variant
- route if route_tag=="high_recall" or eval_score_drop_detected -> float16 (or int8)
- keep int6 for short chat paths and embeddings where latency is critical
add automatic warmstart for sessions >1 request to reduce kv misses.
dan: also add dynamic fallback: if p95 > threshold for a route, circuit-break to int8 for 5 minutes. Implement metric: p95_token_latency_by_route with 1-min buckets.
rebecca: for GTN guidance, provide a simple unit-econ card:
```
scenario A (short chat): int6 -> latency good, cost -40%, quality delta ~0
scenario B (long-doc summarize): int8 -> avoid regressions, cost +20% vs int6 but quality preserved
scenario C (mixed): hybrid routing -> avg cost -25%, tail latency mitigated, guardrails needed
```
samir: experiment plan I can run:
1) run warmstart-enabled perf sweep for int6/int8 on 1024/2048/4096 contexts (batch=1).
2) run eval-suite focusing on summarization + instruction-following with stratified long prompts.
3) collect p50/p95/p99, ROUGE, BLEU, hallucination-rate.
4) compute token-unit-econ with fallback overheads.
I'll produce a short scorecard.
maria: perfect. can you also include a small A/B signal we can show GTN: delta_cost_per_1M_tokens, expected regression probability (based on eval hits), and recommended fallback thresholds.
samir: yes. initial guess numbers (rough):
- int6 baseline cost: $2.1 per 1M tokens
- int8 baseline cost: $3.5 per 1M tokens
- int6 effective (with 25% fallback): $3.0 per 1M tokens
- expected regression prob on long-docs: int6=18%, int8=4% (based on small eval)
will replace with measured after sweep.
rebecca: for rollout notes to GTN: emphasize canary to 0.5% of prod traffic with long-doc monitoring. include automated opt-out to float16 if semantic eval drop >1 pt on a rolling window.
ashok: also flag engineering work: need cheap upstream warmstart API (session token) + runtime metric to tag cache-hit rate per session.
qa-bot: automated test suggestion: add 50 long-doc synthetic cases to CI that must pass coverage heuristics (no more than 2 repeated sections, coverage metric>=0.8).
maria: ok assigning: @samir run perf + scorecard (ETA 48h), @ashok add warmstart + cache metrics (ETA 72h), @rebecca draft GTN card + rollback policy (ETA 24h). I'll collect and present to product on Mon.
rebecca: ack.
ashok: ack.
samir: ack, starting sweep now. will post interim results in this thread. :rocket:
